thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate detected on dedicated cluster cluster-ded-42. 5xx spike (5m avg 7.9%), p95 latency elevated. Source alert: redwood-prod-dedicated-alerts.

sara: Oncall ack. Pulling logs and node metrics for cluster-ded-42 now.

mike: I can already see a lot of connection resets and GPU mem pressure in the aggregated view. Any recent deploys? @deploy-bot can you confirm?

deploy-bot: No deploys to cluster-ded-42 in the last 45 minutes.

priya: Which tenant(s) are showing the errors? Need to scope customer impact.

sara: Grepping request logs -> majority of 5xx have tenant_id=acmefin-prod, route=/v1/dedicated/generate. Error types: 503 read timeout, 504 gateway timeout, and occasional "kernel OOM" in kube events.

leo: Kernel OOMs on GPU hosts points to memory exhaustion per process. Could be a noisy tenant running large-context batches. @ryan can you pull per-node GPU usage and pod list?

ryan: Querying metrics... grafana -> https://grafana/internal/cluster-ded-42/dedicated-overview

ryan: node-gpu-7 GPU memory at 97-100%, repeated evictions. Top processes: llm_worker (pid 4281) owned by acmefin-prod. There are 5 replicas of acmefin-llm pinned to node-gpu-7.

sara: That matches 'noisy neighbour'. Since this is a dedicated allocation, AcmeFin's replicas are allowed to consume full node resources. Immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle their ingress traffic at the API gateway; 2) scale their deployment to 0 on offending node; 3) migrate to a larger dedicated pool; 4) temporarily add spare GPUs. Fastest likely throttle + scale-down.

mike: Throttle first. Priya, alert AE/SE to let customer know and ask to pause heavy workloads if possible.

priya: DMing AcmeFin SRE and AE now. Also preparing a customer-facing status blurb.

sara: Applying temporary rate limit: `rwctl apigw rate-limit set --tenant acmefin-prod --rps 12 --duration 20m`

sara: Rate limit in place. Observability: 5xx dropped from 7.9% -> 3.4% in ~40s, p95 latency down to ~900ms.

leo: Good improvement but node-gpu-7 still showing OOM events for existing pods. We need to stop the runaway processes to avoid repeated churn. Suggest scale acmefin-llm -> 0 then restart in a new pool.

ryan: I'm on node-gpu-7. Listing pods: acmefin-llm-0..4 pinned. Will `kubectl scale deploy/acmefin-llm --replicas=0 -n tenants-acmefin` to stop them. This will drop current in-flight requests. Confirming everyone ok with dropped inflight?

sara: OK to proceed because we've throttled ingress. Proceed with scale to 0.

ryan: Scaled to 0. Kernel OOMs stop, GPU mem freed, node stabilizes.

mike: Next: create new dedicated pool with more capacity (highmem) and deploy acmefin there with reduced concurrency and KV cache limits. Priya can provision or we can use fallback.

priya: I'll provision a new pool: `infractl pool create --name ded-acmefin-hot --gpu a100-80gb --size 4` (est. 8-12m). Or we can redirect to shared fallback pool until it's ready. Which do we prefer?

sara: Prefer dedicated-hot. Start provisioning and then deploy with conservative env overrides to limit memory per worker.

ryan: New pool provisioning started. ETA ~9m.

leo: While waiting, we should avoid complex request replay. Keep throttles and advise clients to retry with backoff.

acmefin-bot: Notified: "Redwood has applied temporary rate limiting and is migrating your workload. You may see reduced throughput while we stabilize. We will follow up with details."

priya: New pool ready. Deploying acmefin-llm with env overrides: `CONCURRENCY=1`, `KV_CACHE_LIMIT=2GB`, `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=1024`.

ryan: Deployment successful, 4 replicas healthy in ded-acmefin-hot.

priya: Rerouting tenant traffic: `rwctl routing set --tenant acmefin-prod --pool ded-acmefin-hot --drain-old 60s` -> applied.

sara: Traffic shifting. Observability: 5xx ~0.4%, p95 ~230ms. No further OOM events.

mike: Incident state: mitigated. Classification: customer-specific noisy neighbor on Dedicated pool causing capacity exhaustion and kernel OOMs on node hosts.

priya: Proposed action items: short-term: enforce per-tenant concurrency and memory caps by default on Dedicated allocations; add automatic tenant-level throttling when cluster p95 spikes; mid-term: automated live migration tooling to move tenants off pressured pools; mid/long-term: circuit-breaker to auto-isolate after repeated OOMs and admin UI for capacity burst requests.

leo: Assignments: sara -> incident timeline and customer comms (ETA 2h); ryan -> temp per-tenant eviction script & infra alerting (ETA 24h); priya -> spec gateway auto-throttle rule (ETA 48h); mike -> coordinate SRE/product on auto-migration design (ETA 1w).

sara: Handoff: ryan will be night oncall watching the new pool for 4h with 30m check-ins. I'll lead postmortem and customer follow-up.

ryan: ACK. I'll monitor and escalate if regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated -> recording participants and timeline. Attach postmortem when ready to close.

sara: Creating DOC ticket DOC-1234 and postmortem draft. Closing this thread when postmortem uploaded.

priya: Filing incident record and notifying product and sales.

mike: Thanks team. Great quick mitigation and coordinated customer comms.
